newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-AUSTRALIAN QUARTET TAKE WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-AUSTRALIAN QUARTET TAKE WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Australia set a men's 4x200 metres freestyle relay world short-course record on Friday, their second relay world mark in two days at the world short-course swimming championships.

Michael Klim, Grant Hackett, Bill Kirby and Matthew Dunn clocked seven minutes 2.74 seconds to beat the mark of 7:05.17 set on February 9, 1986, by a West German quartet of Rainer Henkel, Alexander Schwotka, Dirk Korthals and Michael Gross.
It was Australia's fifth title of the four-day championships and their second world record following the new standard they set on Thursday in the men's 4x100 metres medley relay.
In a fierce finish for the other medals, Sweden were second in 7:05.61 and Britain third in 7:05.81, just 0.09 seconds ahead of Germany.
